text:
devin: Heads-up — we're getting a spike of 500/503s for hosted inference in us-west-2 starting ~08:12 UTC. Customer Jane from Acme opened a support ticket, says requests time out then get 500s.

sasha: I'm seeing the same in SLO dashboards — p50 latency fine, error rate on the api-gateway -> upstr-infer cluster jumps around 08:11. Lots of container restarts on pool-gpu-1.

oncall-nyc: alert: :rotating_light: 3 services impacted: hosted-api, routing-proxy, upstr-infer-usw2 (pods flapping). Paging infra.

opsbot: Deploy bot: New daemonset node-driver-kernel rolled to 4 nodes in us-west-2 at 08:05 UTC.

mike-infra: ok I'm on it. fetching pod logs now.

mike-infra: kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=pool-gpu-1 --show-labels

# NAME                                  READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
infer-worker-7c9b4                     1/1     Running   6          3h
infer-worker-8f2a1                     0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   12   1h
infer-worker-9a1b2                     1/1     Running   0          20m

mike-infra: logs from infer-worker-8f2a1 show repeated driver issues: "CUDA error: device-side assert triggered" then segfault. snippet: 

[2026-03-15T08:10:12Z] model_server.cpp:423] kv_cache_prefetch: OOM when allocating 536870912 bytes
[2026-03-15T08:10:12Z] inference_runner.cc:1123] Unhandled exception: SIGSEGV (code=0x1) at 0x7fffb2c12345
#0  0x7fffb2c12345 in libcudart.so.11+0x8f45

cassie-support: Jane says her requests to model id `open-llama-70b` specifically fail; lower token requests to smaller models succeed. She included a sample request and timestamp. Ticket: SUP-2026-3342.

jane_acme: shared: "request id=7a9b... timestamp=08:11:05; payload size ~6.2kb; latency 4s then 500" — wants ETA.

devin: Important to separate two hypotheses: (1) GPU OOM on large-context requests (batches with long sequences) (2) driver mismatch after kernel rollout causing memory corruption. Logs point to both OOM and SIGSEGV.

sasha: Repro plan: run the customer's payload against a canary in the same pool and with older driver pinned. If it repros only on new driver, rollback.

mike-infra: Spawning a debug pod with same CUDA/container image and `--gdb` attached per instructions: 

kubectl -n inference run debug-repro --image=redwood/infer:prod-2026-03 --overrides='{"spec": {"nodeSelector": {"pool": "pool-gpu-1"}}}' -- /bin/bash

mike-infra: Also pulling kernel/driver versions: infer-worker-8f2a1: nvidia-driver 535.112, libcudart 11.7, container image uses cudnn 8.4. On older healthy node infer-worker-9a1b2: nvidia-driver 530.41, libcudart 11.6.

oncall-nyc: That mismatch could cause device-side asserts if kernels compiled against different ABI. Rolling driver to 535 across all nodes might be safer OR rolling back the recent node-driver-kernel rollout.

opsbot: Rollout record: node-driver-kernel v3.2 -> v3.3 deployed to pool-gpu-1 at 08:04 UTC (strategy: canary 4 nodes -> global).

devin: immediate mitigation steps:
- set the routing policy to fallback to smaller model variant for requests > 4k tokens
- temporarily drain nodes with driver v3.3 from pool-gpu-1 (cordon + evict)
- increase pod restart backoff and set autoscale min replicas + warm caches to avoid cold OOMs

sasha: I've pushed a routing change: requests with sequence_length > 4096 now route to open-llama-70b-quantized or open-llama-13b. Should reduce OOM risk. :white_check_mark:

mike-infra: cordoning nodes with v3.3 now: `kubectl cordon node-az2-03` etc. Evicting pods off the problematic nodes.

mike-infra: After cordon/evict, crashes dropped. infer-worker-8f2a1 restarted on node-az2-01 (driver 530.41) and is stable. Error rate back down to baseline in 3 minutes.

cassie-support: Jane notified. She reported reduced failures after ~08:28 UTC. Marking as partial-resolved for customer.

jane_acme: thanks for quick response — please keep me posted about root cause and whether we need to change model config.

devin: Long-term actions for postmortem:
- revert/validate node-driver-kernel rollout process (add automated smoke tests that run a representative large-context request before global rollout)
- add a driver/version affinity check in scheduler so similar containers land on nodes with compatible drivers
- better heap/kv-cache monitoring to detect pre-OOM growth patterns
- add per-model fallback rules in routing so heavy requests fallback automatically to quantized variants

sasha: I'll own the rollout process change. Mike, can you add driver/version label checks in our placement controller?

mike-infra: yes, I'll open an infra PR and add a forced canary step with smoke tests.

oncall-nyc: tagging incident for postmortem: INC-2026-0452. Assigning Sev2.

opsbot: Incident timeline recorded.

devin: closing thread — tracking in INC-2026-0452 and SUP-2026-3342. Will follow up with postmortem in #postmortems tomorrow. :lock:
